_what: Host-neutral agent control policy (WQ-480). ONE source of truth for two questions: which commands the agent is obliged to run itself rather than hand over, and which decisions the owner has already made. Every host-specific control compiles from this file; none of them owns a copy.
_why_globs: Patterns are GLOBS, not regexes, and that is the whole portability decision. A glob compiles to a regex losslessly (escape, then * -> .*, ? -> .); a regex cannot be compiled to a glob at all. Authoring in regex is what would have locked this policy to the PowerShell hooks that happened to be written first - and OpenCode's native permission layer takes globs, matched against the whole command string. Author once in the form that travels; let each adapter compile.

_compiles_to.cursor: pack/templates/cursor/hooks/shell-preapprove.ps1 and offload-detect.ps1 compile these globs to regex at runtime. No generated file, so there is nothing to go stale.
_compiles_to.opencode: bootstrap-project.ps1 compiles shell.allow / shell.refuse into opencode.json -> permission.bash as a glob->effect map, which is that host's native mechanism. verify-agent-policy.ps1 reports drift between this file and any generated block.

_effect_mapping: allow -> allow. refuse -> ASK, never deny. Refuse here means 'this control has no opinion, let normal review happen' - it is the owner's call, not a prohibition. Compiling refuse to deny would take away the approval the owner is entitled to give.

shell._allow_note: Each entry is something the agent-defaults rule ('Fixes the agent runs - do not offload') already obliges the agent to run in-session. That is the entire basis for pre-approving them: the rule says the agent must not hand these over, so a reviewer stopping them manufactures the excuse the rule forbids. Add a project's own test and build entry points here.
shell._refuse_note: Refuse wins over allow, always. These are either the owner's decision (profile writes, publishing), destructive, or capable of carrying a second command. A prefix match on the allow list must never override an entry here.

_settled_note: WQ-477. An ask that re-raises a decision the owner already made is the same defect as offloading a runnable command, and worse in one way: offloading spends a turn, while re-asking tells the owner their answer did not stick. Each entry names where the decision is recorded so a control can point at the record rather than assert. Add an entry when a decision has been restated more than once; remove one only when the decision genuinely changes.

settled.decision: Publishing, git, and CI require StarterPack-Airlock on the host Desktop with a valid publisher key. Default pack copies are git-free.
